constructor:rack::app::LedDisplaySeparat.finding: P1: no cited test asserts anything about a constructed LedDisplaySeparator; tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:374-397 only constructs it, overwrites its box and renders it with no assertion, so Rack's constructor (box.size = Vec(), src/app/LedDisplay.cpp) and the Python peer are unverified. Smallest fix: assert app.LedDisplaySeparator().box.size == Vec() and isinstance(..., w.Widget).

destructor:rack::app::ModuleLightWidget:.finding: P1: no cited test checks what happens when a ModuleLightWidget is deleted. Rack's destructor removes an open tooltip (src/app/ModuleLightWidget.cpp ~ModuleLightWidget), and the notes say RackPy invalidates the peer and detaches its module link. Yet the tests only call light.close() in finally blocks, with no later assertion (tests/app/in_rack/test_controls.py:140-143, :380-383, :468-469). Smallest fix: create a tooltip, close the light, then assert HOOKS.scene_tooltip_count() fell, not light.alive, and that deleting the module afterwards is safe.

field:rack::app::LedDisplayChoice::bgCol.finding: P1: bg_color is written (tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:379) but never read back or checked through drawing anywhere in the suite, so a broken getter/setter (native/bindings/app/rack.cpp LedDisplayChoice bg_color property) would pass. Smallest fix: assert choice.bg_color == nvg.rgb(0, 0, 0) after the assignment, or assert Rack's default rgba(0,0,0,0).

field:rack::app::LedDisplayChoice::color.finding: P1: color is written (tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:379) but never read back or checked through drawing anywhere in the suite. Smallest fix: assert choice.color == nvg.rgb(255, 0, 0), or assert Rack's constructor default rgb(0xff,0xd7,0x14) before assigning.

field:rack::app::LedDisplayTextField::co.finding: P1: field.color is written (tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:382) but never read back anywhere in the suite. Smallest fix: assert field.color == nvg.rgb(1, 2, 3).

field:rack::app::LedDisplayTextField::fo.finding: P1: field.font_path is written (tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:383) but never read back anywhere in the suite. Smallest fix: assert field.font_path == 'res/fonts/ShareTechMono-Regular.ttf'.

field:rack::app::LightWidget::borderColo.finding: P1: border_color is only written (tests/app/in_rack/test_controls.py:498) and never read back or checked in pixels anywhere in the suite; grep finds no other border_color use. field:rack::app::MidiChannelChoice::port.finding: P1: MidiChannelChoice.port is set, but neither its getter nor its effect is asserted. In tests/app/in_rack/test_io_widgets.py:51-57 the channel choice's text (names[2]) is never checked, and on_action's 'MIDI channel' label (:75) is added even when the port is null (src/app/MidiDisplay.cpp MidiChannelChoice::onAction). Smallest fix: assert c.port is loop and names[2] == loop.get_channel_name(loop.get_channel()).

function:rack::app::appendMidiMenu(rack:.finding: P1: the cited doc docs/reference/app.md:443-446 says Rack 2.6.6's combined MIDI menu has no channel choice. In fact appendMidiMenu adds a 'MIDI channel' submenu item (src/app/MidiDisplay.cpp appendMidiMenu: createMenuItem<MidiChannelItem>("MidiDisplay.channel", RIGHT_ARROW)). The test comment at tests/app/in_rack/test_io_widgets.py:76 repeats the error, because take_scene_menu_labels collects only MenuLabels. The test at :152-155 only checks that the child count grew. Also P2: append_midi_menu rejects port=None (pythonMidiPort, native/bindings/midi.cpp:656-659), which Rack handles by appending labels only; this restriction is not documented. Smallest fix: correct the doc to say channel is a submenu item, and assert the menu's last item text is 'MIDI channel'.

method:rack::app::LedDisplay::draw(const.finding: P1: the only cited exercise is frame.render() at tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:393, with no assertion. Neither Rack's LedDisplay::draw output (dark gradient background) nor rackpy.raw.app.LedDisplay.draw is checked, so a wrong mapping would pass. Smallest fix: read HOOKS.framebuffer_pixels(frame) after render and assert a dark background pixel, as test_controls.py:505-506 does for lights.

method:rack::app::LedDisplay::drawLayer(.finding: P1: no assertion exercises LedDisplay.draw_layer. tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:393 renders a framebuffer with no assertion, and nothing calls or overrides draw_layer on a LedDisplay. Smallest fix: draw layer 1 through a Python container (as test_controls.py:487-491 does) and assert that a child override is reached, or check a pixel.

method:rack::app::LedDisplayChoice::draw.finding: P1: only frame.render() at tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:393 with no assertion. Rack's bg_color fill (src/app/LedDisplay.cpp LedDisplayChoice::draw) is never checked. Smallest fix: give the choice an opaque bg_color, render, and assert the pixel colour.

P1: no assertion exercises LedDisplayChoice.draw_layer. Rack draws text only on layer 1, and the cited test (tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:393) renders layer 0 in a framebuffer without asserting anything. Smallest fix: draw layer 1 explicitly (draw_child(child, args, 1)) and assert pixels in the text colour.

method:rack::app::LedDisplayChoice::onBu.finding: P1: no test anywhere calls LedDisplayChoice.on_button. Rack's override dispatches onAction on a left or right press and consumes the event (src/app/LedDisplay.cpp LedDisplayChoice::onButton), which is untested; grep finds no on_button use on an LED choice. Smallest fix: subclass LedDisplayChoice with an on_action recorder, call on_button with a ButtonEvent (PRESS, LEFT), and assert on_action ran.

method:rack::app::LedDisplaySeparator::d.finding: P1: only frame.render() at tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:393 with no assertion; the separator's line is never checked. Smallest fix: render a separator with a diagonal box and assert a pixel on the line has Rack's #333333 stroke.

method:rack::app::LedDisplayTextField::d.finding: P1: only frame.render() at tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:393 with no assertion on the text field's drawing. Smallest fix: assert that a pixel or a child-draw override is reached after render.

P1: Rack draws the field's text and caret on layer 1, but the cited test renders a framebuffer (layer 0) with no assertion (tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:393). Smallest fix: draw layer 1 explicitly and assert text-coloured pixels.

method:rack::app::LedDisplayTextField::g.finding: P1: the only assertion, 0 <= field.get_text_position(Vec(30, 10)) <= 3 at tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:385, accepts every valid result for the 3-character text, including Rack's no-font fallback 0. A mapping to ui::TextField::getTextPosition or a constant would pass. Smallest fix: assert distinct positions, e.g. get_text_position(Vec(0, 10)) == 0 and get_text_position(Vec(59, 10)) == 3.

method:rack::app::MidiButton::onAction(c.finding: P1: the cited doc docs/reference/app.md:443-446 says the button's combined MIDI menu has no channel choice. Rack's MidiButton::onAction calls appendMidiMenu, which adds a 'MIDI channel' submenu item (src/app/MidiDisplay.cpp). The test passes only because take_scene_menu_labels collects MenuLabels (native/testing/testing.cpp:870-874), and its comment 'Rack's combined menu omits channel' (tests/app/in_rack/test_io_widgets.py:76) is wrong. Smallest fix: correct the doc and the comment to say the channel is a submenu item.

method:rack::app::MidiChannelChoice::ste.finding: P1: MidiChannelChoice.step() runs in tests/app/in_rack/test_io_widgets.py:51-57, but its text (names[2]) is never asserted, and no other test checks it. Rack's step sets the text to port->getChannelName(port->getChannel()), or to the 'channel 1' string without a port. Smallest fix: assert names[2] == loop.get_channel_name(loop.get_channel()), and assert the no-port text.

method:rack::app::ModuleLightWidget::onH.finding: P1: no test anywhere calls on_hover on a ModuleLightWidget. The cited tests (tests/app/in_rack/test_controls.py:356-384 and :436-469) never send a HoverEvent. Rack's override consumes the event only when the light has a LightInfo (src/app/ModuleLightWidget.cpp onHover), and that is untested. Smallest fix: call light.on_hover(w.HoverEvent(...)) with and without a configured LightInfo, and assert whether the event was consumed.

record:rack::app::LedDisplay.finding: P1: no test asserts anything about rackpy.raw.app.LedDisplay itself. tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:374-397 constructs it, adds children and renders without an assertion, and the notes' claim that it can be subclassed is never exercised. Smallest fix: subclass LedDisplay with a draw override that calls super(), render, and assert the override ran and Rack's background was drawn.

record:rack::app::LedDisplaySeparator.finding: P1: no test asserts anything about rackpy.raw.app.LedDisplaySeparator. In tests/app/in_rack/test_rack.py:374-397 it is only constructed, given a box and rendered. MidiDisplay's driver_separator is Rack's own instance seen as a host view, not this class.
